boundaries.label: Headless core — WALL: no process, fs, ink, @/tui
Adapters + platform — the only OS branch

cards.title: The layers — references/cli-architecture.md §1
items: domain owns entities, rules and pure types; it imports nothing platform-specific — no process, no fs, no Ink, no SDK
core owns use cases, orchestration, ports and the event stream; it imports the domain and the ports, never the UI
commands parse, validate, call the core and map the result to an output and an exit code; the TUI renders the same core through its public API
adapters implement the ports (terminal, shell, filesystem, secrets, config, updater); platform is the only place allowed to branch on the OS
contracts holds the output schemas, the event envelopes and the exit codes, and imports nothing else

cards.title: Ports, not imports — references/cli-architecture.md §2 and §3
items: the consumer declares the port, the adapter implements it: OutputPort and TerminalPort, ShellPort, SecretStorePort, ConfigPort, ClockPort, SdkClient, UpdaterPort, TelemetryPort, OpenerPort and ClipboardPort
a use case that needs 'the API' depends on SdkClient, not on the generated client module
bin/main builds the container lazily — config, secret store, SDK, output port, clock — and the fast path (--version, --help) does not build it
commands receive the container; they never construct adapters. The TUI receives the core's public API and the terminal port; it never builds the SDK
tests build the same container with fakes, so the use case does not change between production and test

cards.title: The unbreakable rules — README.md §The architecture contract
items: stdout is data; stderr is diagnostics — nothing else writes to stdout except the output port
the core never touches a terminal: no process, no @/tui, no @/commands — the engine is a library
commands never import @/tui — a command runs headless; the TUI is a separate frontend
exit codes and output schemas are contracts: a change is a version bump, not an edit
terminal state is restored on every exit path, including a crash and a signal

cards.title: The machine gates — lints/eslint.config.mjs
items: the layer walls are pinned by path: no-restricted-globals bans process and no-restricted-imports bans fs, node:fs, child_process, node:child_process, ink and the @/tui, @/commands patterns on src/core/** and src/domain/**
the command wall is pinned separately: ink and @/tui are banned on src/commands/** — a command is a headless frontend
no-console makes stdout go through the output port; no-eval, no-new-func and no-implied-eval make remote code impossible; no-debugger keeps the breakpoint out of the build

the type rules are pinned too: ban-ts-comment (a @ts-expect-error needs a reason), switch-exhaustiveness-check, consistent-type-imports, explicit-module-boundary-types, no-unnecessary-type-assertion, no-floating-promises and no-misused-promises
silencing is itself a finding: eslint-comments/no-unlimited-disable and require-description — fix a lint rather than silencing it
